key_insight: GeONet improves flow-field prediction by explicitly encoding solid--void geometry, letting an operator network generalize better across heterogeneous porous media domains.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, geometry-aware pressure prediction for microfluidic design, tracer interpretation, and digital-twin workflows in subsurface energy and critical mineral applications.
method: Extends Branch--Trunk operator learning with a Leaf Network for binary geometry masks.
Uses porosity/permeability inputs plus coordinates, local geometric descriptors, and random Fourier features.
Fuses representations with a gated DeepMixer to predict steady-state pressure fields.
evidence_signal: Trained on 5,000 PFLOTRAN simulations (~30 TB) and validated against pore-scale/Stokes and held-out geometries, GeONet reached NRMSE 0.0381--0.0500 and R^2 0.9673--0.9822, clearly outperforming the DeepONet baseline.
watch_item: Performance depends on high-quality geometry-encoded training data, so generalization to unseen pore structures may still require careful domain coverage and hyperparameter tuning.
paper_title: GeONet: Geometry-Encoded Operator Network for Predicting Flow in Heterogeneous Porous Media
